title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, the space industry is buzzing with a mix of international collaborations and ambitious commercial ventures. From satellite IPOs to new defense partnerships, the landscape is shifting—though not without its hiccups.

themes.title: International Collaborations Heat Up
themes.body: The upcoming ESA-China SMILE mission underscores the growing trend of cross-border partnerships in space exploration. Such collaborations may be the key to tackling complex scientific challenges, but they also highlight geopolitical nuances.

themes.title: Commercial Ventures on the Rise
themes.body: Virgin Galactic's reaffirmation of its commercial service plans signals a cautious optimism in the space tourism sector. Meanwhile, Cowboy's audacious proposal for 20,000 orbital data centers raises eyebrows and questions about the sustainability of such ambitions.

themes.title: Defense Spending Gets a Boost
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adding $1.4 billion to space resilience reflects a growing recognition of space as a critical domain for national security. As threats evolve, so too does the funding landscape, with companies like Anduril and L3Harris vying for lucrative contracts.

themes.title: IPO Activity Signals Market Confidence
themes.body: Chinese satellite maker MinoSpace's $736 million IPO attempt suggests a renewed appetite for investment in space ventures. This comes amid a broader trend of defense-tech companies eyeing the public markets, hinting at a potential thaw in the IPO freeze.
